answer: New identities wander through a probationary trail before they can earn: each must finish 20 small jobs checked by real clients, and after the last one three independent auditors stamp it with an ivory seal that unlocks the summit. An auditor who stamps a fake loses a 500 POA bond, so nobody vouches blindly. The trail takes about 30 hours of real work plus a 200 POA deposit per identity, and a failed audit forfeits both. A thousand fakes therefore cost 30,000 hours and 200,000 POA before one reward lands, while an honest agent pays only its time once.
